title: Affiliate Recruitment Software: How to Find, Recruit, and Keep Affiliates
summary: Compare affiliate recruitment software, agencies, and marketplaces like Fiverr, with pricing, pipeline and outreach workflows, and a decision framework for brands.
body_markdown:
## The Find, Reach, Manage, Measure Workflow: A TikTok Shop Worked Example


A TikTok Shop recruiting workflow connects discovery, outreach, sample handling, follow-up, and performance review. Consider a DTC brand launching a product. The team defines its target creator, contacts prospects with a relevant offer, sets a sample limit, then tracks which partners keep posting and generating GMV. Recruitment software connects work that might otherwise be scattered across spreadsheets, messages, and sample forms.


### Find: build a ranked creator pipeline from a plain-English brief


Start with the product, audience, and content style you want, then describe the ideal partner in plain language. A skincare brand, for example, might look for TikTok Shop creators who make ingredient-focused routines for shoppers interested in sensitive-skin products. Reacher ranks its database of more than 4 million TikTok Shop creators using a[plain-English description](https://www.reacherapp.com/features/creator-discovery) , transcript, product image, or lookalike creator.


Review ranked prospects for fit before outreach. Check their content, audience relevance, and visible product-promotion style, then add qualified creators to a pipeline. A clear brief gives your team a consistent basis for selection and campaign reviews.


### Reach: personalized DM and email outreach at daily volume


Once the prospect list is ready, match the channel and offer to the campaign. Reacher supports outreach through DM, Target Collab, and email, with capacity of up to 10,000 creators per day. Personalized Outreach drafts a unique message using details such as the creator’s name, content, product fit, selling points, and offer. Teams can control tone and preview the message before it sends.


For the skincare launch, the message can refer to a creator’s relevant routine and explain the product offer directly. Keep the call to action clear, and use reply status to guide follow-up. Volume matters, but relevant messages and organized conversation history help the team manage outreach with care.


### Manage: sample funnel math, caps, and re-engagement


Set a weekly sample cap before invitations go out, then assess requests against campaign fit and available inventory. Track each stage: requests received, requests approved, samples shipped, and creators who post. Sample conversion is calculated as creators who post divided by samples shipped. Use actual campaign data rather than assuming a standard rate.


A shared[sample queue](https://www.reacherapp.com/features/sample-management) makes pending requests visible and supports bulk rejection and weekly caps. The creator CRM keeps status, messages, samples, and GMV together. When a creator stalls, Re-engage supports follow-up, helping the team distinguish a delayed post from a relationship that needs a fresh offer.


### Measure: cohort retention and sample economics after the first post


After the first post, evaluate more than immediate sales. Compare creators by cohort, meaning the group recruited during the same month, and track whether members continue posting. Review GMV alongside samples shipped and creator activity to see which recruitment sources and offers produce sustained participation.


Compare sample costs with resulting creator activity and sales to assess sample economics. The dashboard includes cohort retention and sample economics, helping teams identify where to adjust selection, follow-up, or sample allocation. Keep the review grounded in observed data: early performance is a signal for the next decision, not a guarantee of future sales.
